cells.tense: Right now the false thing is falling and you know why it fell, because it fell from something you saw clearly, not something you forced.
cells.ask: Try picking one habit that already keeps your seeing sharp — a short daily pass over what matters — and tend it on purpose this week. It keeps your eye clear when nothing dramatic is falling.
cells.core:
Right now the false thing is falling and you know why it fell, because it fell from something you saw clearly, not something you forced. That is what this looks like when it is going well: you walk into a room, a plan, a mess of other people's certainty, and before you have reasoned it out you know which part matters and which part is scenery. The knowing arrives first; the explanation catches up later. What's left standing after the fall is what you actually attend to, and you're attending to it well.

That seeing needs feeding or it dulls. A small practice kept on purpose — solitude that connects you to your own eye instead of isolating it — keeps the clear view clear when nothing dramatic is falling. Refinement, not fret, is what keeps it lit.
cells.sheetLine: You cleared what couldn't hold and you're looking at what matters, steadily. A short practice kept on purpose is what keeps this sharp.
cells.verb: clearing away what was never built to hold
cells.place: where you know what's worth attending to before you can say why

cells.tense: You're already bracing for the next thing you'll tear down, and the tearing has stopped waiting for anything to actually be wrong.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you're mid-tearing-down and hand it to another person whole — ask them what it means to them, and let their answer stand for a while. Belonging to something unbroken is the training.
cells.core:
You're already bracing for the next thing you'll tear down, and the tearing has stopped waiting for anything to actually be wrong. Every structure looks like a false one if you look long enough, so nothing gets to stand — including you. You arrive at a thing already knowing how it will fall, and you say so before anyone asked, and the room goes quiet in a way you keep mistaking for agreement. The clearing has become the thing it came to clear.

What holds you is being among people who carry something forward together. Ask one person what a thing means to them and let their meaning be real without auditing it. Belonging to something unbroken — even for an afternoon — is the training that puts the wrecking back in your hands instead of ahead of you.
cells.sheetLine: You're tearing things down before anything's gone wrong. Ask someone what a thing means to them and let it stand there.

cells.tense: Something already stopped holding a while back, and you are still the one holding it up, so it looks fine to everyone but you.
cells.ask: Build one small structure on purpose — a plan for next week, a way one meeting runs, a form for the thing you keep improvising — and let it hold by itself for a week without propping it. Structure that serves what it holds frees the eye that was holding it up.
cells.core:
Something already stopped holding a while back, and you are still the one holding it up, so it looks fine to everyone but you. When this is going well it is the opposite: you see straight through to the point of a thing, you drop what has done its job without a second thought, and your attention lands where it will actually matter. People bring you the tangle and you hand back the one thread that counts.

The holding is doing the work your seeing used to do, and the seeing has gone quiet behind it. Give one corner of your life a real shape — a plan, a standing order, one thing that runs the same way every time — and let the shape carry it instead of you. Clear, reliable form is what returns your attention to what matters, because it's what stops you spending attention on holding things upright.
cells.sheetLine: You're holding up something that quit holding a while back. Build one small structure that stands without you.

cells.tense: You're already sorting what matters from what doesn't — in what you give time to, what you let go, what you keep picking back up — you just call it being busy or being practical.
cells.ask: Notice one thing your attention keeps returning to, and let it pull you into one step forward, taken because it drew you, not because it was on a list.
cells.core:
You're already sorting what matters from what doesn't — in what you give time to, what you let go, what you keep picking back up — you just call it being busy or being practical. Handled well, this looks like a person who is hard to distract: they walk past the urgent thing to the important one without a speech about it, and everyone else's noise quiets in their company. The sorting is real. You are doing it right now, in this room.

Whatever structure that sorting has been quietly undermining is going to fall soon, and you'll say it fell on its own. Attention that keeps pulling you toward one thing is the earliest form of the seeing, before it's named. Let it move you one step, and the step tells you the thing was already yours to choose.
cells.sheetLine: Your attention already knows what matters — you're calling it busyness. Follow it one step and own the choosing.
